finding.EMAIL_DMARC_POLICY_NONE.title: DMARC policy is not protective enough
finding.EMAIL_DMARC_POLICY_NONE.summary: A DMARC record exists but is configured as p=none.
finding.EMAIL_DMARC_POLICY_NONE.meaning: DMARC helps determine whether email sent in your domain's name really belongs to you. Your current setting (p=none) only reports; it does not stop spoofed email from reaching recipients.
finding.EMAIL_DMARC_POLICY_NONE.info: This setting does not put your domain directly at risk, but in phishing attacks spoofed email can be sent in your name.
finding.EMAIL_DMARC_POLICY_NONE.fix: For stronger protection, once you are sure your domain is ready, raise the policy first to p=quarantine and then to p=reject.
finding.EMAIL_DMARC_POLICY_NONE.fix_succ: A correctly configured DMARC record protects your domain's reputation and largely blocks spoofed email.
